question.problem:
Negate the following statement:

$\,$ For all $m\in N,$ $3m+1$ is not odd.
question.worked_solution:
If we denote

$$
P(m):3m+1\text{ is odd},
$$

our statement can be written as

$$
∀m\in N,\,¬P(m).
$$

Negating this, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(∀m\in N,\,¬P(m)) & ≡∃m\in N,\,¬¬P(m) \\  & ≡∃m\in N,\,P(m).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $∃m\in N,\,P(m)$ reads as follows:

$\,$ **There exists** $m\in N$ such that $3m+1$ is odd.
